summary: Samuel Ross Winans was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who earned his A.B. at Princeton University (~1870–1874). He served at Princeton as Professor of Greek and Instructor of Sanskrit (1876–1883) and later as dean of the faculty (1899–1903).

Samuel Slater was an Indologist educated at King's College London. He served as Rector at St. Paul's School, Darjeeling (1850), Professor at Bishop's College, Calcutta (1850–1863), Professor of Hindustani at King's College London (1861–1862), and headmaster of Bishop Cotton School (1863–1886).
Samuel Swinton Jacob was an engineer active in history and archaeology. He was educated at Cheam School (~1856–1857) and Addiscombe Military Seminary (~1857–1858).
Samuel Tickell worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary (1827–1829) and subsequently served in the Bengal Army (~1829–1868).
Samuel Wells Williams was a scholar in sinology and linguistics who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (~1831–1832). He later held a post at Yale University (~1877–1884).

Samuel William Fallon worked in linguistics and Indology, earning a Ph.D. from Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1862). He served as an inspector of schools for the Bengal Education Department (~1857–1878).

Sandamali Udeshika Dissanayaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (2017–2021) and the University of Kelaniya (2023–2024). She served as a Temporary Lecturer at the University of Ruhuna in 2024.

Sandeep Namdev Dhikale works in Indology and religious studies, holding an M.A. in Sanskrit from Savitribai Phule Pune University. His posts include Assistant Professor at Fergusson College (2018–2019) and MIT World Peace University (2019–2020).
Sandford Arnot was an Indology and linguistics scholar. In 1826, succeeding John Borthwick Gilchrist, he served as a teacher of Hindustani at the Oriental Institution, Leicester Square.

Sandford Arthur Strong studied at King's College London, under Cecil Bendall, at St John's College, and Oxford. A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, he served as Cambridge's Lecturer of Assyriology (~1894–1903) and UCL's Professor of Arabic (1895).

Sandra A. Wawrytko is a scholar in philosophy, sinology, and Buddhist studies. She held positions at San Diego State University, where she is attested as Professor in 1999 and Associate Professor of Philosophy in 2014.
Sandra Bell is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and served there as a professor in 1991.

Sandra Hochwarter is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned a Magistra der Philosophie from the University of Vienna, where she studied under teacher Anne MacDonald and MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Sang-Kyun Sun is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Delhi under doctoral supervisor Sanghasen Singh (attested 1995). He served as a lecturer at JinGak Buddhist College (attested 1995).

Sanga Tenzin, active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied at Navodaya Education Trust (2012–2016). After working as a clinical nurse (2018), he became HoD and Assistant Professor of Nyingma Sampradaya Shastra at Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Sangay Dorji works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Tengtho Monastery and Semtokha Rigney School, he taught at Semtokha Rigney School, served as Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission (attested 1999–2004), and was a Specialist at the Ministry of Education and Skills Development (2022).

Sangeeta Abhay Patil works in Indology. She earned an MD from Savitribai Phule Pune University (2005–2007) and served as an Academic Consultant at Yashwantrao Chavan Maharashtra Open University in 2023.

Sangharakshita, who worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies, founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967. He studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1949–1950) and under teachers Jagdish Kashyap, Dhardo Rinpoche, Chien Ming Chen, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Sangseraima Ujeed is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2013–2018) and held a Robert H. N. Ho postdoctoral fellowship in Buddhist Studies at UC Santa Barbara (~2018–2020).
Sangye Tenzin was a scholar in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who served as Abbot of Menri Monastery and was attested as a doctoral student at the University of Virginia in 2026.
